title: Leather for the earth
hookLine: you can't answer every bad take online; Shantideva can't pave the earth in leather, but he can wear sandals
tomorrow: anger is rising and the words are coming. what does a log do?

cards: Somewhere online, right now, someone is wrong. A bad take, a rude comment, a stranger misunderstanding something you care about. You could answer every one of them.
People try. It never ends, because there's always another. Shantideva had his own version of the problem, and his answer is a picture you can stand in, quite literally.

teach.b: Difficult people, he says, are as endless as space; you could never overcome them all. Then the picture.

teach.h: NO LEATHER FOR THE WHOLE EARTH.
teach.b: Where would you find enough leather to cover the whole earth, so the stones and thorns never hurt your feet? Nowhere. But put leather on the soles of your own feet, and it's as if the whole earth were covered.
So with the world, he says: I can't hold back everything outside, but I can hold back my own mind. That's the guard from yesterday, given shoes.
Now the week, in six lines. Guard the vow: a promise is a flame you cup. No hands, no feet: craving borrows yours.
They can go: ancient isn't forever. Stand firm: feet down, don't bow. Where would it live: look, and the urge has no home.
Guard the mind: one guard keeps them all. And today, the one that makes the rest walkable.

how: Tibetan and other Mahayana teachers often quote Shantideva's leather verse when teaching that practice works on one's own reactions rather than on changing everyone around.

games.q: what does “leather for the earth” mean?
o: covering the ground so nobody ever gets hurt again
a gift of sandals given to traveling monks long ago
guarding your own mind instead of trying to fix the world

games.q: the week's lines — tap the pairs.
p: a promise is a flame you cup
look, and the urge has no home
guard your mind, not the whole world

s: the leather verse says the world's problems don't matter
it says you can't control everything outside, so you guard your own mind.
Shantideva says difficult people are as endless as space
you could never overcome them all; overcome the mind instead.

games.q: a group chat keeps sharing jokes that sting you a little. you can't control what they post. what's the leather-on-your-feet move?
o: reply to every joke until they finally see your side.
work on how you meet the jokes: notice the sting, choose your reply.
leave every group chat, so nothing can sting again.
games.why: you can't pave the earth. Shantideva guards the one place he stands: his own mind. speaking up is still allowed, from a guarded mind.

practice: Stand up and walk slowly for about a minute, indoors or out, shoes or bare feet. Feel each sole meet the ground: heel, the outer edge, the toes.
Every step lands on something you didn't choose and can't smooth out, and your feet carry you anyway.

wordCard.voice: Leather for the earth: Shantideva's sandal picture. You can't cover the world, so you guard where you stand.

orig.note: Sanskrit: mind, heart; what Shantideva guards in chapter five. Pali citta.

carryVoice: The line for this one: leather on your feet, not on the whole earth. A week of Shantideva on care and watchfulness, done.

sources.ref: Bodhicaryavatara 5.12-5.14 (unruly beings are endless as space; no leather to cover the earth, but leather on the soles covers it; I cannot restrain external things, but I will restrain my mind)
